```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r attach}
library(priogridR)
```

PRIO-GRID cell identifiers increase from west to east and then from south to
north. The utility functions in this vignette expose that indexing convention
and make local neighborhood operations explicit.

## Identifier matrices

`pg_create_indices()` creates a matrix with north at the top, as grids are
normally displayed, even though numbering starts in the south-west.

```{r indices}
indices <- pg_create_indices(nrow = 3, ncol = 4)
indices
```

The south-western cell is therefore in the bottom-left matrix position.

```{r orientation}
indices[3, 1]
indices[1, 4]
```

## First-order neighbors

`pg_neighbors()` returns queen-contiguity neighbors: cells sharing an edge or
a corner with the selected cell.

```{r interior-neighbors}
pg_neighbors(6, nrow = 3, ncol = 4)
```

Longitude wraps across the antimeridian by default. Latitude does not wrap
across either pole.

```{r edge-neighbors}
pg_neighbors(1, nrow = 3, ncol = 4)
pg_neighbors(1, nrow = 3, ncol = 4, wrap_longitude = FALSE)
```

Set `wrap_longitude = FALSE` for regional grids whose eastern and western
edges should not be treated as adjacent.

## Connect IDs to locations

For configured grids, `pg_coords_from_id()` and `pg_geometry()` translate
these abstract identifiers into centre coordinates or spatial features.

```{r geometry}
config <- priogrid::pg_config(nrow = 18, ncol = 36, verbose = FALSE)

pg_coords_from_id(1:3, config = config)
pg_geometry(1:3, geometry = "point", config = config)
```

See `vignette("grid-foundations", package = "priogridR")` for coordinate
assignment, panel validation, completion, safe joins, and mapping.
